classification.difficultyReason: Combine the perpendicular-bisects-chord property with Pythagoras, then double the half-chord length.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: Circle with centre O on the perpendicular from the top circumference point to the lower horizontal chord. The complete perpendicular segment is labelled 12 cm, the sloping chord to the right endpoint is labelled 13 cm, and x labels the complete horizontal chord. Ordinary source colours are replaced by house black.
spec.mathematics: The perpendicular through the centre bisects the horizontal chord. Each half is the remaining leg of a right triangle with hypotenuse 13 cm and vertical leg 12 cm. Coordinates satisfy both the circle incidence and the right-triangle lengths.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and x are visible; the supplied 10 cm answer is omitted.

answer.worked:
The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord. Let each half have length $h$.
$$\begin{aligned}h^2+12^2&=13^2\\h^2&=169-144\\h&=5\text{ cm}\\x&=2\times5=10\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$$
